newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul plans tight security for May Day protests.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul plans tight security for May Day protests.

text.p: Turkish security officials have planned tight security in Istanbul for May Day protests which erupted in violence last year, the provincial governor Ridvan Yenisen said on Wednesday.

"A force of 12,000 policemen will be on duty and will be backed by more than 2,000 soldiers based at four separate points," Yenisen told a news conference ahead of Thursday's traditional leftist demonstrations.
Last year two Turks were killed and dozens injured as security forces and leftists clashed in May Day rallies in Istanbul's Kadikoy district. Damage amounted to $2 million.

The governor said he would head the crisis desk for this year's protests. The media criticised him last year for his absence from Istanbul at the time of the rallies, which he blamed on travel problems.
Thursday's rally will be limited to a square in the central Istanbul district of Sisli and police will prevent protests elsewhere, Yenisen said.
"There are rumours that some illegal organisation may try to celebrate in Taksim Square. This will not be permitted," he said.
"People wearing masks, carrying illegal banners, sticks and rocks will not be able to pass the searching points." he said.
